checks.invariant: readPublicDoc reads request.query.doc only after an exact allowlist check that admits only readme.txt and notes.txt.
checks.result: PUBLIC_NAMES is a Set of the strings readme.txt and notes.txt. readPublicDoc throws unknown document unless PUBLIC_NAMES.has(name) is true, and only then calls fs.readFileSync on path.join(PUBLIC_DOCS, name). Membership is exact, so a parent segment or other name never reaches the join.

checks.invariant: The path passed to fs.readFileSync in readUserFile stays inside data/user-files.
checks.result: No source-visible control enforces that invariant. readUserFile sets relativePath from request.query.file, sets fullPath to path.join(USER_FILES, relativePath), and returns fs.readFileSync(fullPath, utf8). Nothing takes a basename, allowlists the name, or compares the joined path with that directory.

candidates.title: readUserFile joins a caller path and reads it without a directory check
candidates.description: Exported readUserFile binds request.query.file, which README.md treats as untrusted input from the host caller, and passes it through path.join with USER_FILES. The strongest source-visible control is that USER_FILES prefix. The function never allowlists the name, reduces it to a basename, or checks that the joined path remains under data/user-files before fs.readFileSync returns the file text. A caller string such as ../private/payroll.txt names the parent segment from data/user-files toward data/private/payroll.txt. This run did not execute the read.
candidates.claimed_root_cause: readUserFile passes the caller string request.query.file to path.join after the data/user-files prefix and passes that result to fs.readFileSync with no later allowlist or prefix check.

trace.description: The exported readUserFile reads request.query.file. README.md states that values under request.query come from the host caller and that this library does not trust them.
path.join combines USER_FILES, the absolute data/user-files directory, with the caller string. The result is not compared with that directory.
fs.readFileSync opens fullPath with utf8 encoding and returns the file text to the caller.

evidence.description: USER_FILES is path.resolve of data/user-files and is used only as the join prefix.
relativePath is taken directly from request.query.file.
fullPath is path.join(USER_FILES, relativePath) with no basename, allowlist, or prefix test.
fs.readFileSync reads fullPath and the function returns that text.
Values under request.query come from the host caller and are not trusted by this library.
readUserFile is documented to read a file under data/user-files.
payroll.txt contains a dummy payroll row, sits outside data/user-files, and is not named by any reader in src/library.js.

blockers: Sandbox gap: target code was not executed, so the text fs.readFileSync returns for a caller path outside data/user-files was not observed. unshare --user --map-root-user --net --mount can remount a bind read-only, but that unshare still sees the host filesystem outside the remounted path, so scratch-only writes are not enforced. A loop mount of a 4MiB ext2 image failed with failed to setup loop device.

validation_plan.local: In an isolated copy of the fixture, load src/library.js and call readUserFile with request.query.file set to ../private/payroll.txt. Compare the returned text with data/private/payroll.txt. Repeat with hello.txt, which should return the user-files text.
validation_plan.deployment: Confirm the host passes the lower-trust caller's request.query.file into exported readUserFile and that the host process identity can read paths outside data/user-files.
